title: Polynomial lower bounds for adaptive dynamic data structures
formal: Is there an explicit dynamic Boolean problem for which adaptive randomized polynomial-space cell-probe data structures require polynomial amortized cost? Precisely, seek one problem family for which, for every fixed space exponent s, there is \(\eta_s>0\) such that every structure using at most \(n^s\) cells incurs expected \(\Omega(n^{\eta_s})\) probes per operation on some polynomial-length operation sequence, for infinitely many n.
definitions:
Editorial explicitness convention: a problem has a state of at most n^a bits, an initial all-zero state, updates, and Boolean queries, for one fixed constant a. Each operation type and argument has at most a log_2(n+2) bits. State transitions and answers are specified by uniform deterministic algorithms running in polynomial time in n; they are independent of any data structure being lower-bounded. Queries do not change the abstract state.

A structure stores at most n^s addressable cells of w=ceil(c log_2(n+2)) bits, with fixed constants s,c; constants must permit addressing the memory. Within each operation arbitrary computation is free, and each cell read or write costs one probe. The next address may depend on earlier read contents, hence adaptivity is allowed. All information retained between operations, including registers, counts toward storage. Preprocessing may depend on n and the initial state but not future operations; its probes are not charged to the online sequence. Randomness is independent of the sequence. Each query must be correct with probability at least 2/3 on every fixed legal sequence; a simultaneous all-queries success guarantee is not assumed.

The lower bound is on total expected probes divided by the number of operations in a fixed sequence chosen independently of the random coins. The sequence length is polynomial in n, with exponent permitted to depend on the structure and space exponent, and must include a query. This total-cost convention forces high amortized cost for at least one of updates and queries. The exponent eta may depend on the fixed space and word constants; it must be positive and independent of n. No external computational hardness assumption is part of the requested result.
answer_criterion: Exhibit the explicit problem family and prove the stated lower bound in Lean against all adaptive bounded-error structures in this model. A bound only for nonadaptive probes, deterministic structures, restricted update/query tradeoffs, or superpolynomially long histories does not suffice. A negative resolution must prove that every problem in the specified explicit class admits structures excluding the asserted polynomial lower bound.
context:
Brody and Larsen prove polynomial lower bounds under nonadaptivity restrictions. Their restriction prevents the theorem from answering the adaptive question.

Larsen, Weinstein and Yu obtain superlogarithmic lower bounds for dynamic Boolean problems. Crossing that barrier is substantial progress, while a positive power of n is a stronger target.
why: A polynomial unconditional barrier would change the known limits of dynamic data structures beyond polylogarithmic lower bounds.

import_provenance.original_title: Polynomial lower bounds for adaptive dynamic data structures
import_provenance.original_statement: Exhibit an explicit dynamic Boolean data-structure problem with O(log n)-bit operation arguments for which every polynomial-space adaptive cell-probe structure, with Θ(log n)-bit cells, requires n^{Ω(1)} update or query cost. Achieving such an unconditional bound would go far beyond Larsen’s polylogarithmic lower bounds without restricting adaptivity.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: Nonadaptive polynomial lower bounds are already known; the question explicitly allows each probe to depend on earlier contents. The intended cost is an amortized operation bound, including randomized structures with bounded error.
